sn51.22:1.2: It is typical of Ānanda to ask the Buddha on such matters. Here he elicits from the Buddha a fascinating and unique description of his meditative methods for developing special abilities.
sn51.22:1.5: In several cases he is said to have disappeared from where he was and reappeared in the realm of divinity (eg. SN 6.5, MN 49:3.2), but I am not sure if it is possible to determine which method he used in specific instances. It seems reasonable to infer that this was his ordinary physical body, because he disappeared from his normal place. A mind-made body is a separate entity (MN 77:30.1), so the physical body should remain where it is. On the other hand, the same expression is used when he approached Anuruddha, who explicitly says it was a mind-made body (AN 8.30:23.3).
sn51.22:2.1: Omāti is a unique verb, literally to “measure down”. The commentary treats it as pahoti, “is able”. The past participle omatta is occasionally found in the sense of the lesser or subordinate option (Tha Ap 146:4.3; DN-a 2:214.105). Notice that up until now, in both Ānanda’s questions and the Buddha’s answers, the phrasing has been exactly parallel. Ānanda is varying the phrasing here. I think he means to suggest that the mind-made body is the less impressive power, so I translate “is at least able”.
sn51.22:4.1: On the physics of this see DN 23:17.5.
